open_issues: Spec text said the recovery code is '20 chars + 1 checksum char' displayed as '5 groups of 4', which cannot both hold (21 characters do not fit into 20 slots). Implemented as five dash separated groups 4-4-4-4-5, with the check character riding at the end of the last group (XXXX-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX-XXXXC). Change RecoveryCode.Group if the owner wants a different grouping.

PairingQrPayload carries an extra issuedAt field beyond the five fields the spec listed (orgId/officeId/pcDeviceId/pcX25519Pub/token); without it the phone side cannot evaluate the ten minute window from the QR image alone.

DeviceCertificateBody has no explicit expiry field (the spec fixed the field list), so CertificateChain.Verify treats 'expired' as (a) issuance dated more than one day in the future and (b) an optional maxAge freshness window the caller supplies. If the owner wants a notAfter field in the signed body, the format must be extended before the first setup file ships.
No packages were added; Directory.Packages.props, Directory.Build.props and Wakeel.slnx were not touched.
notes:
Design decisions worth knowing for the packages that build on this one.

FORMATS
- Aead buffer layout: [version:1][nonce:12][ciphertext][tag:16]; the version byte and the caller's associated data are both authenticated, so re-labelling or downgrading a blob breaks decryption.
- Aead stream layout (used for container payloads): [version:1][chunkSize:4] then frames [final:1][nonce:12][length:4][ciphertext+tag]. Each frame's associated data includes the caller AD, the big endian frame index and the final flag, and the stream always ends with an explicit empty final frame, so truncation, reordering and frame splicing are all detected. Default chunk 1 MB; backups never need to fit in memory.
- Container = ZIP with payload.bin (chunked AEAD of an inner ZIP of the entries), manifest.json (canonical JSON) and signature.bin = Ed25519 over sha256(manifest bytes) || sha256(payload bytes). ContainerReader.Open verifies signature, then the certificate chain and revocation, then the expected kind, the format version and createdAt <= now + 1 day, all before a payload byte is touched; decryption happens later in ReadEntries/ReadEntry/ExtractTo, which additionally re-check each entry's recorded size and SHA-256.
- Manifest hashes are the plaintext hashes of the entries, lower case hex. The signature is over the raw manifest bytes as stored, not over a re-serialised manifest, so an odd byte in the file can never be normalised away.

KEY SEPARATION
- Every symmetric key is used through a labelled sub key: office and session keys go through HKDF with "wakeel.container|<kind>", so the same office key produces different keys for a sync packet and a phone packet. Key wraps bind their associated data to "<context>|<kind>|v1", so a DbKey wrap cannot be opened as a VaultKey wrap.
- SealFor is a sealed box: ephemeral X25519 public key (32 bytes) || AEAD blob, with HKDF salt = ephemeralPub || recipientPub and info = "wakeel.seal|<context>"; that salt is also the associated data. Agree() orders the two public keys in the salt so both sides derive the same session key without knowing who started.
- Argon2 failures are mapped to WrongPassword (not Tampered) at the key wrap layer and for password mode containers, so the UI layer can say the right thing; a wrong office/session key stays Tampered.

TIME
- Everything time dependent takes a TimeProvider: container writing and reading, certificate verification (explicit DateTimeOffset now), pairing expiry, installation file timestamps, and Argon2 AutoTune (GetTimestamp/GetElapsedTime). Nothing calls DateTime.Now.
- AutoTune probe limit is targetMs * 1.5, which is the specified 1500 ms at the default target of 1000 ms; it starts at 64 MB / 3 / 2 and halves memory, never below 32 MB, and returns parameters with a fresh salt.

CANONICAL JSON
- camelCase members, ordinal key sort, no whitespace, enums as lower camel names ("pc", "phone", "msg", "officeKey"), instants forced to UTC with millisecond precision, byte arrays as standard base64 (public keys and signatures are base64url strings instead), nulls omitted. Every signed body goes through it, so two machines produce identical bytes.

FILE SAFETY
- InstallationKeyFile.Save writes a .tmp, copies the previous file to .bak, then moves the temp over the target; no Windows only call is used (no DPAPI here). The Desktop host supplies the DPAPI IPlatformProtector later; NullPlatformProtector is present only so tests and non Windows builds can exercise the machine wrap path and is documented as not secure.

TEST COVERAGE (136 tests): primitive round trips and negative cases, AEAD tamper/truncation/wrong-AD/wrong-version/wrong-key, streaming at 0/1/4096/300000 bytes, Argon2 determinism and both AutoTune branches, recovery code grouping, normalisation, and the mathematically complete single character check, canonical JSON stability and ordering, all four wrap kinds plus wrong password/wrong code/wrong context, installation file round trip with .bak, device seeds under the DbKey, Ed25519/X25519 round trips and sealed boxes, certificate chains valid/forged/wrong issuer/missing parent/revoked/future dated/too old, all seven container extensions, four payload modes, tampering of manifest, payload and signature separately plus a re-signed tampered payload, a 3 MB streamed backup, and the full pairing exchange from QR to a verifiable phone certificate.
